page: Vultr vcg-a40-2c-10g-4vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance belonging to the Cloud GPU family. It features an x86_64 Intel CPU with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core and 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 10.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core. For acceleration, it bundles a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU (0.0833 allocation) with 4 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 180 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a clear division between general-purpose compute and GPU-accelerated workloads. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance and single-threaded compression/decompression tasks rank in the average tier. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and Passmark CPU scores fall into the weak category, reflecting the low core count and 2.0 GHz clock speed. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also weak to poor. Conversely, LLM inference benchmarks show strong performance, with prompt processing reaching 3480.67 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 202.17 tokens per second for a medium 7B model.

This instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full, dedicated GPU. By slicing the NVIDIA A40 GPU into a fractional resource with 4 GB VRAM, it provides a budget-friendly profile for lightweight machine learning tasks. It is best suited for small-scale LLM inference, model prototyping, lightweight CUDA development, and basic graphics rendering. It is less appropriate for memory-intensive databases, high-throughput web serving, or heavy multi-threaded CPU compilation.
